No Man´s Sky PC review - Not as good as it should and could be

When it achieves "could be" I'm in! I wanted to believe and preorder it. But, I have been dissapointed before. I'm done with preorders. I will wait for the release review, the patch, the fix, and finally the good review before I buy. The problem is I like everything about this game based on the hype. I can wait.

I like it quite a bit. I really like survival, inventory managment type shit though. I can definitely see why the hardcore gamer and multiplayer gamer crowds would be disappointed by this title, but it hits most of the points I wanted it to pretty well.

I do have some complaints though. It's a bit buggy. I've played worse, and I honestly expected this at launch. At the start of the game, there are way too few inventory slots, but I have 43 slots in my suit now (each slot holds maximum of 250 of each resource), my ship has 27 (holds 500 per slot), and my gun has 14 slots. After getting the inventory up a bit there is a lot more exploration before I go find a trading post/space station to pawn everything off at.

I would have also liked to have seen cities. There are occasional outposts that have three or four occupied buildings, but that's about it. The universe feels a bit empty.

I would also like to see some interaction between the games three races (which is being hinted at a bit, so we'll see how that holds up.)

There is plenty to do in the game, and it's one of the best sandboxes I've played. It does not do everything that was promised.

The scale of the thing is mindbogglingly big. Open the galaxy map and try to zoom to the center if you haven't already. I quit after about ten minutes, and had only went about 20k - 30k light years. The galaxy seems to be about 400 k light years across, with the center being about 200 k light years.
I think people just overhyped it and set their expectations way too high. I would really hate to be a game developer today having to serve the self righteous crowd

This is exactly what happened. The authors spent a lot of time trying to show everyone exactly what the game was about, but nobody wanted to believe it. Everyone else had their own predefined idea about what a space game should be and chose to believe that NMS would be that game. Hello games didn't overhype the game, gamers did that themselves.

I feel bad for Hello Games in all of this, because despite the knee-jerk reaction many will have from only a few short hours of play they did actually create something very ambitious that has a neat story. However you need to play the game long enough to begin to experience and appreciate those things.

This is not and was never meant to be a game for the person who is easily bored. It's a game for the explorer.

I'm moderately interested in the game (I knew very little about it before it came out other than people screaming about how it would be the most amazing game ever) and I think you're spot on. It almost makes me want to pay full price to support the developer.

I am actually really enjoying it right now. I'm not a very hardcore gamer, so something that just involves exploration and a bit of crafting and fighting now and again is entertaining to me. That's what I expected it to be. Everyone thinking "OMGZ you're gonna shoot all the aliens and the action will be so intense and I bet you can time travel and make your own planets and blow them up!!" obviously hasn't been watching Sean Murray's demonstrations at events like E3. They didn't go back on any promises. They delivered exactly what they said they would, and everyone's bitching about it. That would be like seeing a poster for a new movie with Nicolas Cage's face right there in the center of the poster, then you go see the movie and you give it a bad review because you hate Nicolas Cage. For people saying the game's boring, well, to each their own. I find games about exploration and crafting entertaining, but not everyone else will. I find MOBAs incredibly boring, yet those are some of the most popular games out right now.

As for the bugs, yeah that sucks. I'm able to play with no issues, but for those who can't get the game to work on their systems, yeah that's probably something you should be mad about. But for people bitching about how the gameplay was pretty much exactly what was shown to us...you're not very bright, are you?
